{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script (translated from LSF)

# LSF requested:
#   -W 16:00
#   -n 8
#   -M 48000
#   -R "span[ptile=8]"
#   -e logs/train_scratch%J.err
#   -o logs/train_scratch%J.out
#   -q amdgpu
#   -gpu "num=1"

flux alloc \
  -n 8 \
  --gpus=1 \
  --time=16h \
  --queue=amdgpu \
  bash -lc '

mkdir -p logs

# Approximate LSF %J with Flux job id.
exec >"logs/train_scratch${FLUX_JOB_ID}.out" 2>"logs/train_scratch${FLUX_JOB_ID}.err"

# NOTE: LSF -M 48000 (memory limit/request) has no universally portable Flux directive in a batch script.
# Performance implication: without a memory request/limit, the job may be placed where less memory is available,
# increasing risk of OOM or contention.

# NOTE: LSF -R "span[ptile=8]" has no universally portable Flux directive.
# Performance implication: task placement/packing may differ, which can affect performance.

module load bedtools/2.29.2-wrl
module load gcc/9.3.0
module load cuda/11.7
module load samtools/1.6-wrl
module load pigz/2.6.0
module load ucsctools
source activate maxatac

cd /data/weirauchlab/team/ngun7t/maxatac/runs

maxatac train --genome hg38 \
  --arch Transformer_phuc \
  --sequence /users/ngun7t/opt/maxatac/data/hg38/hg38.2bit \
  --meta_file /data/weirauchlab/team/ngun7t/maxatac/training_data/meta_file.tsv \
  --output /data/weirauchlab/team/ngun7t/maxatac/runs/scratch \
  --prefix scratch \
  --epochs 1
'
"
}
